questions.questionText: What does a conditional edge's routing function receive and return?
options: It receives nothing and returns a random node
It receives the current state and returns a string naming which node to go to next
It receives the graph definition and returns a new graph
It receives only the very first user message
questions.correctAnswer: It receives the current state and returns a string naming which node to go to next
questions.explanation: A conditional edge is a plain function of state that decides where to route based on whatever the state currently contains.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between a "loop" and "routing" in a LangGraph graph?
options: A loop is a normal edge pointing back to an earlier node; routing is a conditional edge choosing between multiple possible next nodes
Loops can only be used with tool nodes
Routing can only happen at the START node
questions.correctAnswer: A loop is a normal edge pointing back to an earlier node; routing is a conditional edge choosing between multiple possible next nodes
questions.explanation: tools -> agent going back to reprocess is a loop (fixed destination); agent -> {tools | END} deciding which path to take is routing (conditional destination).

questions.questionText: In the conditional edges mapping object passed to addConditionalEdges, what is it used for?
options: It's optional decoration with no functional purpose
It maps the strings your routing function can return to the actual node names in the graph
It defines the initial state of the graph
It sets the maximum number of loop iterations
questions.correctAnswer: It maps the strings your routing function can return to the actual node names in the graph
questions.explanation: This indirection lets a routing function's output values stay decoupled from specific node names, so the same function can be reused across differently-structured graphs.
